claims.text: TC4 has low hardness and poor wear behavior under high-contact stress.
A MoNbTaW-based refractory high-entropy-alloy coating will be deposited on TC4 by HiPIMS.
The coated TC4 will be annealed at approximately 500 degrees Celsius for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere.
HiPIMS will produce a uniform, dense RHEA film on TC4.
The intervention will form a nanocrystalline and compositionally homogeneous coating.
The RHEA coating will be strongly bonded to the TC4 substrate.
The RHEA's multi-principal-element composition and nanostructure will impart very high hardness.
The RHEA's multi-principal-element composition and nanostructure will resist plastic deformation.
Annealing at 500 degrees Celsius will enhance coating-substrate bonding and relieve residual stress.
The annealing treatment will not form deleterious intermetallic phases.
The hard, deformation-resistant coating will shield the softer TC4 substrate and thereby reduce friction and wear under high stress.
The coating and annealing treatment will preserve TC4's beneficial bulk properties.
Relative to untreated TC4, coated and annealed samples will have significantly greater surface hardness.
Relative to untreated TC4, coated and annealed samples will have a lower coefficient of friction under high-contact stress.
Relative to untreated TC4, coated and annealed samples will have a lower wear rate under high-contact stress.
The coating is expected to remain effective at temperatures up to approximately 500 degrees Celsius.
Above approximately 500 degrees Celsius or outside the tested contact-stress range, coating degradation or interface failure may occur.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on coating composition, deposition conditions, and annealing parameters.
